description.value: Ten-ee-ah Lodge is a remote wilderness resort on Spout Lake in the Cariboo region of BC, founded in 1942 as a hunting base camp and now offering log cabin accommodations, camping, and a European-inspired restaurant with West Coast cuisine and local craft beer. The only property on Spout Lake and situated 1,077 metres above sea level, it is accessed via 21 km of maintained gravel road and caters to an international clientele, particularly from Europe. Touring cyclists willing to make the remote approach will find a full-service destination with on-site dining, canoeing, kayaking, and hiking.

address.value: Spout Lake Road, Lac La Hache, V0K 1T0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is fully accessible and provides comprehensive resort information including 2026 rates, confirming the lodge is currently operating despite banners seeking new managers and new ownership. Neither the website nor OSM tags mention secure bike storage, cycling-specific services, or any of the other required criteria, so those remain null. OSM tags include internet_access=wlan but the website does not confirm WiFi, so that amenity is null per the rules; the on-site restaurant and lounge are clearly described as serving dinner, confirming nearby evening food.
concerns: Homepage prominently displays 'Looking for new managers' and 'Looking for new ownership' banners; news page confirms the Bader Family is stepping down after 24 years and the lodge is for sale — operational continuity is uncertain.
Physical location is 30 km northeast of Lac La Hache with the last 21 km on maintained gravel road — very remote access that may deter or be impractical for many touring cyclists.
OSM street address (Spout Lake Road) differs from website mailing address (P.O. Box 157, Lac La Hache) — not contradictory but address confirmation is partial.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The lodge is operating with 2026 rates posted, but is actively seeking new managers and is listed for sale, creating real uncertainty about near-term continuity; the WWC directory should verify operational status before including. Additionally, no cycling-specific amenities are evidenced, and the 21 km gravel access road makes this a challenging destination for touring cyclists rather than a service stop.
enrichment_extras.notes: Campground offers both powered (15 amp) and unpowered sites with fire pits, free firewood, picnic tables, and access to lodge showers — could appeal to cycle-camping tourers. Lodge has a rich history dating to 1942 and caters heavily to European guests.

Nearby evening food.detail: On-site restaurant and lounge serving European-inspired West Coast cuisine with 3-course dinners on a patio overlooking Spout Lake; full bar with Okanagan wines, Canadian whiskeys, and local craft beer on tap
